speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started and if you have experienced any recent trauma or insect bites to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury is very concerning for a flexor tendon injury, possibly a jersey finger. Can you try to actively flex your right ring finger at the distal joint, and does it feel like it catches or locks when you move it?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint following a forced extension injury is highly suggestive of a flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion, commonly known as Jersey finger. To confirm the diagnosis and assess for bony avulsion fragments, I need to visualize the tendon and bone structure. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_right_hand REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound_right_hand_finger

text: RESULTS: X-ray_of_the_Right_Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger. Ultrasound_right_hand_finger: NORMAL READINGS

text: The ultrasound showing normal readings is unexpected given your symptoms, so I need to look closer. Can you try to make a fist again while I observe if the finger fails to bend, and is there a palpable defect or gap at the base of your fingernail?
